content.text:
We have a Game of Thrones board game scenario: House Greyjoy in round 6, phase resolve-single-march, with March order at Moat Cailin (id: mô?), order id 2 March +0. The action guidance shows legal reachable regions from Moat Cailin, which are:

- greywater-watch (land, castle-level 0, no castle, controller greyjoy, no combat)
- seagard (land, castle-level 2 (stronghold), controller greyjoy, no combat)
- the-twins (land, no castle)
- white-harbor (land, castle-level 1 (castle), controller null)
- winterfell (land, castle-level 2 (stronghold), controller Stark, garrison 2 (garrison token of Stark? Actually Stark's home area includes Garrison 2), triggersCombat true.

The "castleAreasLostIfEmptiedWithoutToken": 1 for Moat Cailin (since it's a castle area, moving all units out without leaving a power token loses control of the castle area, we lose 1 castle area). And "canLeavePowerToken": true (we can spend 1 power token to preserve it).

We have two units at Moat Cailin: ids 6 (knight), 37 (knight). So an army of 2 knights.

Supply track: Greyjoy supply is 3. That means permitted army sizes? Supply 3 gives armies allowed: 3,2,2,2 (as per supply table). So we can have up to 4 armies: one of size ≤3, three of size ≤2. Each army must have at least 2 units. The 2 knights currently form an army of size 2. So after moving, we must ensure that any army we create conforms to supply constraints.

If we move both knights together into a destination that already has a friendly army (units of same house) we would merge. If we move to empty territory, they'd form a new army possibly size 2 (still counts). If we leave one knight behind (i.e., split), then we still have a single knight at Moat Cailin (unit 6 or 37). A single unit does NOT count as an army (according to rules). However having a single unit left is allowed. But we must be careful: leaving 1 knight alone at Moat Cailin while moving the other somewhere else gives a single unit; that means we have only an army of size 2 (the moving knight maybe ends up alone: if it moves to a region without other units, it forms a single unit (size 1) which is NOT an army – that's allowed but doesn't count for supply? Actually supply only limits armies (size >=2). So if you move a single knight alone into a new area by itself, that unit is not an army, so it's fine – you can have a "loner" unit as per supply constraints. However, you cannot leave single knights alone in Moat Cailin as an army because it's not an army, but you can vacate the area leaving no units. But you need to consider the power token option: if you move both knights out, vacating Moat Cailin entirely (no units left) you must place a power token to keep control, else you lose the castle area. You can also leave one unit there (so control remains automatically due to unit presence; you would not lose castle). Then you wouldn't need a power token. But note Moat Cailin is a castle area (castle=1). Actually Moat Cailin has castle=1 (as per map). Use that for victory points: currently a castle area controlled (counted). If you leave a unit there, you still control the castle area because you have unit. So no need to spend power token. However, moving both units out while leaving a power token also retains control but costs a power token.

Now we consider possible moves:

- Move to greywater-watch which is already controlled by Greyjoy (no castle area). That's safe, no combat, no castle gain. Moves: could move both knights together (they are already there, they are friendly). That swings no combat and no castle gain. We would keep castle at Moat Cailin if we leave at least one unit there. If we move both, we must leave a power token to keep control (cost token). Might be wasteful.

- Move to seagard: also controlled by Greyjoy (currently no units, but castle area controlled from seagard? Seagard is a stronghold (castle=2). Actually in map, seagard is "castle=2; supply=?" The map indicates seagard [land; castle=2] meaning it's a stronghold. Greyjoy controls it already (controlPowerToken? actually seagard controlPowerToken is "greyjoy"? Indeed board entry for seagard shows controlPowerToken: "greyjoy", no units. So no units there but have control token? Actually board entry: "seagard" controlPowerToken: "greyjoy". So Greyjoy controls seagard, presumably by having placed a power token there earlier (or units?). So it's a stronghold (castle=2). So you already count that as a castle area in your victory points: yes, "controlledCastleAreas":4 includes seagard as stronghold maybe counted. So moving units into seagard would not gain a new castle area (already have). No combat. Could be good to consolidate, but also we might not need to move.

- Move to the-twins: not controlled. No castle.

- White Harbor: castle area, not controlled. Capturing would give a castle area without combat (if no enemy units). Since it's not occupied, moving units there would capture (controlPowerToken set to Greyjoy). There's no defending units. So we could move there without combat. Also no enemy garrison (none). So we could get a castle area (white harbor is castle=1) if we move there.

- Winterfell: enemy stronghold with defenders: Stark units: there is a knight unit? Actually winterfell has one footman (id 33) and a garrison of 2. No other units. Also there is a ship (id 34) from Stark present (but it's a ship located at bay-of-ice not winterfell). So winterfell is defended by a single footman, a garrison token of strength 2. Also the board shows a garrison value 2 (the usual garrison of winterfell). There's no house card yet (that would add strength). So to capture winterfell we must have enough combat strength to defeat the defender with the footman plus garrison plus possibly support.

We also need to consider support that can be called in from adjacent areas that contain a Support order. The reachable destinations include winterfell (triggersCombat true). If we move there, we may start combat; we can call for support from adjacent areas with support orders belonging to any house (including us) that have a support order placed. Let's see what adjacent support orders are present around winterfell: Adjacent areas to winterfell are: bay-of-ice (Consolidate Power order, not support), castle-black (Support +0), karhold (Support +0), moat-cailin (March), port-of-winterfell (?? not in board?), the-shivering-sea (sea), the-stony-shore (land), white-harbor (none?). Actually check map: Winterfell connects to bay-of-ice, castle-black, karhold, moat-cailin, port-of-winterfell, the-shivering-sea, the-stony-shore, white-harbor. So which of those have Support orders? We have:

- castle-black: Support +0 order (regionId castle-black, orderID 7). Yes, support order present: "Support +0".

- karhold: Support +0 order (regionId karhold, orderId 8). Yes, support.

- moat-cailin has March order, no support.

- bay-of-ice has Consolidate Power.

- port-of-winterfell unknown (no order listed; maybe none).

- the-shivering-sea no order (sea, might be no order; likely none).

- the-stony-shore no order.

- white-harbor no order (though may have unit? Actually white-harbor is empty. No support order.)

So we have potential support from castle-black (Stark), karhold (Stark). However, those are both Stark units: castle-black has two knights (Stark) but also support order is placed; a support order can be used by any house? Actually support orders belong to the player who placed them (the house controlling the area and who placed the order). The support orders are placed by the respective house in the planning phase. So castle-black support order belongs to Stark (since the region is controlled by Stark, they placed the order). Similarly karhold support order belongs to Stark. So if we attack Winterfell, Stark may choose to provide support to themselves (defender). They have a support order; they will decide to support themselves in the combat; they'll have all units in castle-black and karhold add to defender combat strength (though they are not adjacent? Actually support is from adjacent area to the embattled area; castle-black and karhold are adjacent to winterfell, so yes they can support.

Thus if we attack winterfell, Stark can give support from both areas. And they have knights at each location: castle-black has two knights; karhold has one knight. So defender's units: footman (1 strength) + garrison 2 = 3 base. Plus support: each knight adds 2 combat each. So total defender strength: 3 + 2+2+2 = 9. Actually garrison is 2 (strength), footman 1 => 3, plus knights 6 => 9 total.

We as Greyjoy have 2 knights (strength each 2) for 4 strength, plus March order strength (the March order is +0). Also we have a possible support from Greyjoy adjacent to winterfell? Check adjacent Greyjoy's support order? There's no support order placed by Greyjoy near winterfell, but greyjoy does have a support order at Greywater Watch but that area is not adjacent to winterfell (Greywater Watch is adjacent to Moat Cailin? Let's check map: Greywater Watch connects to Moat Cailin, flints-finger, etc. Not adjacent to winterfell. Also flints-finger not adjacent. So no support from Greyjoy to winterfell. (Also we have no other support order in neighboring area to winterfell.)

Thus attacking winterfell seems hopeless. So we wouldn't attack winterfell.

What about moving to white harbor? Since no enemy units present. That's a direct capture (no combat). White harbor is a castle area (castle=1). Thus moving any number of units there will capture it (give control token). There's no combat, no support needed. We may leave it unoccupied proper? The rule: If a player moves units into an area with only a power token (or none) and no enemy units, then they take control; any power token there is discarded. So moving two knights into white harbor would give us castle area. That would increase our castle count to 5 (since we currently have 4: Pyke stronghold (castle=2), Ironman's Bay not a castle, seagard stronghold, maybe also Greywater Watch is a castle? Actually greywater-watch is castle=1, so is a castle area. Wait map: greywater-watch [land; castle=1], so yes it's a castle (always controlled). So we have castle areas: Pyke (stronghold), Greywater Watch (castle), Seagard (stronghold), maybe also another castle like castle=1 somewhere else - check controlledCastleAreas: currently 4. Which ones? Likely: pyke (stronghold), seagard (stronghold), greywater-watch (castle=1), maybe one more: the get from description: greyjoy's controlledCastleAreas=4. Looking at board, the other castle/stronghold under Greyjoy's control is "Ironman's Bay"? That's not a castle. "Port of Pyke"? no. Moat Cailin is a castle (castle=1). And indeed they own Moat Cailin castle=1. So the four are: Pyke (stronghold), Seagard (stronghold), Greywater Watch (castle), Moat Cailin (castle). So capturing White Harbor (castle) would increase to 5 (plus also losing Moat Cailin if we vacate it). But we can preserve Moat Cailin by leaving a power token (cost 1). That yields net gain of +1 castle area (gain White Harbor, keep Moat Cailin). Or if we move both knights to White Harbor and also leave a power token, we net +1.

If we move them to White Harbor AND also leave a power token, we keep Moat Cailin's castle, so gain extra castle. If we move both knights and do not leave a token, we lose Moat Cailin but gain White Harbor; net no change (0 net). If we move only one knight to White Harbor and leave the other at Moat Cailin; then we keep Moat Cailin (no token needed) and we have one knight left (solo unit) at Moat Cailin, still control castle (unit present). So we also gain a new castle at White Harbor (control token placed). That gives net +1 castle area (gain White Harbor). This costs no power token. However we must consider supply: leaving a single knight at Moat Cailin is not an army; the other knight is at White Harbor alone (also not an army), so no army constraints are violated (no armies). That's allowed. However, is it legal to have a unit in a castle area with no other friendly units? Yes. That's fine.

Thus best is to move only one knight to White Harbor, keep the other at Moat Cailin, and not spend a token; gain 1 castle area net.

However we must also consider possible support for White Harbor? No combat, no support required. That's simple.

Also, moving to white harbor may have an enemy adjacent? White Harbor is adjacent to moat-cailin (source) and also (maybe) to other areas like The Narrow Sea (sea) and The Shivering Sea, etc. But no opponent units there.

Thus likely optimal move: move unit(s) to White Harbor (capture). Choose to move only one knight (id 6 or 37). But we must also follow rules about "Supply safe unitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone": The reachable region info includes "supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone": [[6], [37], [6,37]]. That indicates any grouping of unit(s) is safe supply-wise. So moving a single unit is okay.

Thus we can set moves: one group moving unit 6 to white-harbor, and maybe we could also move unit 37 somewhere else? But we are limited to at most 2 destinations (max 2 moves). The order's reachable destination list can include multiple groups. However we could also move a second unit to perhaps greywater-watch or seagard etc. But moving extra unit may not be beneficial. Let's think: If we move both knights to white harbor, you would have both knights there, forming an army of size 2 (valid). Then Moat Cailin would be empty, we'd need to decide whether to leave a power token. You could also leave it empty and not place a token (losing control). That would net you: lose Moat Cailin castle, gain White Harbor castle = net 0. Not good. Could also place a token to keep Moat Cailin, pay token, net +0 castle (gain White Harbor but pay token, lose no castle). Similar to moving one unit, but cost token.

Thus moving one unit to capture white harbor while leaving the other at Moat Cailin (no token needed) yields +1 castle and also retains both units. That seems best.

But we have to consider that Moat Cailin is a castle; we have a March order; if we move one unit out, the area still has a single knight, which does not count as an army; but does moving a unit out from a castle area under control by a unit cause losing control? No, control is retained as long as at least one unit remains in the area. So we keep control of Moat Cailin.

Thus we can set:

moves: [
 {destination_region_id: "white-harbor", unit_ids: [6]}, // move knight id 6
 // could also have second move group for maybe moving other unit somewhere but optional. But we have max 2 moves. If we want to also move unit 37 maybe to greywater-watch? That would be okay (since it's a friendly area). But moving unit 37 somewhere else might waste potential later moves, or weaken defense at Moat Cailin (but we have no more March orders there). Might adjust supply? No.

May we leave unit 37 at Moat Cailin, which is okay.

Thus we should set moves with only one group. According to the schema, moves array can have up to 2 items. So we can provide one group.

leave_power_token: false (since we keep one unit, no need to spend token).

Now we must ensure that moving a knight to white harbor triggers ability: the area is a castle (castle=1), no enemy units, so we place a control token (or automatically take control?). The rule says if you move into an area with no enemy units, you take control. Since we have no power token there, we just capture.

Now we need to consider if there is any enemy presence in white harbor (the board shows white-harbor has no units and controlPowerToken null). So we can capture.

Now we need to check any restrictions about moving to a castle area that is not adjacent but reachable via the path listed. Yes, white-harbor is listed as reachable region.

Thus final answer: moves: [ {destination_region_id: "white-harbor", unit_ids: [6] } ], leave_power_token: false.

Alternatively, could also move unit 37. Choose either. Also verifying that unit 6's id is a knight belonging to Greyjoy. It should be okay.

Now we have to consider if we might want to also move the second knight to white harbor as well (both into same destination) because we can move multiple units to same region. The reachable region data's "supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone" includes [6,37] group meaning both moving together is also safe. But we prefer to move just one.

Potential downside: Having a single knight left at Moat Cailin may be vulnerable to later attacks, but it's a castle area, garrison? No garrison. But can be taken by enemy attacks later if they move there with enough force. However at the moment, scoring this castle is more urgent as we want to win quickly. Keeping a unit there might be valuable for defense. Might also be necessary for future moves (like using support). But we have support orders at castle-black and karhold (Stark) not Greyjoy.

Alternatively, moving both knights to white harbor could free up Moat Cailin to potentially be perished but we would have both knights at White Harbor. That secure both castles: white harbor (new) and Moat Cailin lost. We might consider the future: Moat Cailin is a castle, but losing it reduces our controlled castles from 4 to 3 if we take white harbor, net is 0 change. But we currently have 4 castle areas. To win we need 7. So each additional castle is important. Losing Moat Cailin is undesirable. Thus moving only one knight seems best.

Thus final answer.

We need to ensure that we correctly specify the unit IDs to move. The unit IDs present: 6 and 37. Both knights.

Thus final JSON.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. You choose which remaining March area to resolve now. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
